page: Microsoft Azure EC64as_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ECasv6 family, powered by AMD processors and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This virtual machine features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying instead on external storage options, with explicit support for Premium Storage.

Operating with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads. The lack of local storage means all disk operations depend on network-attached storage, which represents a tradeoff in terms of local I/O latency but offers flexibility in storage scaling. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density provide a stable resource profile for enterprise workloads without the overhead of unused local NVMe drives or GPU hardware.

This hardware configuration is suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and in-memory analytics. The 512.0 GB memory capacity and dedicated 64 vCPUs also support heavy virtualization, large-scale caching layers, and data-processing pipelines that require substantial RAM without requiring local scratch space.
